title: ee.daemon.response.v1
description: Length-prefixed JSON response envelope returned by the optional `ee daemon` Unix-domain socket RPC introduced by bd-oja31 (SRR1 hot-mode skeleton). The wire framing matches `ee.daemon.request.v1`: 4-byte big-endian unsigned length followed by exactly that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON. `request_id`, `agent_id`, and optional `workspace_id` echo the request. Exactly one of `result` or `error` is populated. `ee.daemon.capabilities` advertises envelope schemas, methods, authorization, and nested `method_schemas`; clients must fall back locally when `ee.daemon.search` or compatible request/response schemas are absent. A successful search result is the strict `ee.daemon.search.response.v4` wrapper around canonical `ee.response.v2` machine output, optional canonical `ee.explain.performance.v1` output requested through `ee.daemon.search.request.v2`, human output, an honest reuse contract, and nondeterministic daemon/search phase timings. The daemon process and default embedder are process-scoped. Immutable vector readers are generation-scoped; source admission still runs per request, and WAL-bearing or unverifiable artifacts use uncached readers. Updated clients also accept the unchanged v3 per-request-index contract from an older running daemon.

request_id.description: Echo of the request envelope's request_id. A response whose request_id does not match the most recent request on the same connection MUST be treated as a framing error and the connection torn down.

agent_id.description: Echo of the request envelope's agent_id. Pre-parse refusal responses use a sentinel such as `<unknown>` because the daemon could not safely read the caller's envelope.

workspace_id.description: Echo of the request envelope's optional workspace_id when present. Absent when the request omitted it or when the daemon refused before parsing the request envelope.

result.description: Method-specific payload. Capability results include `protocol`, envelope schemas, methods, authorization, `method_schemas`, and forward-compatibility policy. Current search results use strict `ee.daemon.search.response.v4`; the historical v3 schema remains available for compatible older daemons. Write results use `ee.daemon.write.v1`: `success` describes the durable source write. A committed memory carries `entityId`, `workspaceId`, `workspacePath`, `persisted: true`, `indexJobId`, `indexStatus` (indexed, queued, or failed), `reportStatus` (complete or unavailable), `remember` (the full canonical ee.response.v2 remember report, or null if post-commit reporting failed or the complete response would exceed the frame limit), and structured `degraded` entries with repair guidance bound to the quoted workspace path. Oversized reports and variable degradation details are replaced by a compact successful acknowledgement with a bounded follow-up warning; envelope and exact acknowledgement capacity are admitted before source commit. Queued/failed indexing or unavailable reporting never changes a committed memory to success:false; clients must repair the named job or inspect the existing memory rather than repeat the source write. Journal/outcome acknowledgements retain their success/entityId shape.

error.description: Populated when the method failed. Registered codes include `daemon_unknown_method`, `daemon_method_unauthorized`, `daemon_request_decode_failed`, `daemon_request_schema_mismatch`, `daemon_context_params_invalid`, `daemon_context_deadline_exceeded`, `daemon_context_execution_failed`, `daemon_search_params_invalid`, `daemon_search_execution_failed`, and `daemon_pack_search_feedback_unsupported`, plus method-specific write, telemetry, lifecycle, and authorization codes. The feedback code refuses retrieval-only pack handoff when the workspace feedback ledger is nonempty; it is a method error and CLI fallbackReason, not a new degraded code. Consumers must tolerate unknown codes and opt-in CLI clients must use canonical local search when daemon search fails.

degraded_codes.description: Bare degraded-code strings the daemon attached to the response. The CLI client maps each entry onto a full `ee.response.v2` `degraded[]` entry (severity/repair pulled from the canonical taxonomy in docs/degraded_code_taxonomy.md). Empty array when nothing degraded.
